terms.gloss: chronological order, the order of time
terms.comment: “In chronological order” is an ablative absolute, servātō temporis ōrdine, “the order of time being kept”. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: ordo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 291.
